summary: HDL carries cholesterol away from the arteries and back to the liver. Because of that direction of travel, a higher HDL is generally read as protective — the opposite of how LDL is read.
what_it_measures: The concentration of cholesterol carried in high-density lipoprotein particles, reported in mmol/L.

interpretations.meaning: A low HDL is associated with higher cardiovascular risk, particularly when triglycerides are raised at the same time.
A high HDL is usually unremarkable, though very high values are not necessarily more protective than moderately raised ones.

when_to_seek_help: HDL is only meaningful as part of a full lipid profile and an overall risk assessment. Discuss the whole panel with your GP.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
